name: Patagotitan
sum: Patagotitan is a giant titanosaur from the Cretaceous Cerro Barcino Formation of Patagonia, known from at least six young adults.
wsnote: Revised estimates in the cited Wikipedia revision; early press figures of 37 m and 69 t were later reduced.
holotype: MPEF-PV 3400, a skeleton from the site FLV3, chosen because it was the best preserved.
material: At least six young adult individuals from the Cerro Barcino Formation.
biology: The 2017 analysis placed it as sister to Argentinosaurus, joined by long neural spines in the front back vertebrae.
author: Carballido et al. 2017

images.caption: Mounted cast of Patagotitan at the Field Museum.

sources.text: J. L. Carballido, D. Pol, and A. Otero, I. A. Cerda, L. Salgado, A. C. Garrido, J. Ramezani, N. R. Cúneo, J. M. Krause. 2017. A new giant titanosaur sheds light on body mass evolution among sauropod dinosaurs. Proceedings of the Royal Society of London B 284:20171219:1-10
